title: The Ultimate History of Video Games, Volume 1
author: Steven L. Kent
vetoReason: Specialist historical review by Ethan Johnson documents repeated source-handling failures: executive recollections and promotional interviews are used without adequate dating or challenge, and the Kassar dismissal narrative is treated as established despite contrary evidence. The problem affects the recurring account of industrial decisions and success, beyond incidental errata.
note: Mandatory Karpathy coverage. History of creative technical production passes H7; not a games manual. Original production was The First Quarter (2000), revised and retitled in 2001; no reset of P14. This review concerns volume 1 only. Johnson acknowledges valuable interviews and broad chronological coverage, and readers strongly enjoy it; those defenses do not cure the evidence failures. US-centered reporting concerns an internationally influential industry, so T11 is not automatic. Technology production is central, not media commentary under T12. Not selected.

title: The Age of Cryptocurrency: How Bitcoin and Digital Money Are Challenging the Global Economic Order
author: Paul Vigna and Michael J. Casey
vetoReason: The central transformation narrative relies on an overstated removal of trust and intermediaries. Eric Posner directly challenges that foundation: reliance shifts to software, governance and service providers. Tim Swanson's chapter-level critique independently disputes adoption metrics and the inference from the protocol to broad financial replacement. These are central causal claims, beyond merely outdated prices.
note: Mandatory Karpathy coverage. General history and analysis, not investment instructions or specialist training. Munger's positive review and Swanson's praise for the electronic-money history and prose preserve substantial counterfactual value. They do not establish the claimed removal of institutional trust. Veto concerns foundations, not cryptocurrency as a topic. Finance is central, T12=-10; global scope gives T11=0. Paperback subtitle changes Digital Money to the Blockchain; same work. Not selected.
notes: Good historical reporting mixed with unsupported adoption and institutional-replacement claims.

title: Rationality: From AI to Zombies
author: Eliezer Yudkowsky
note: Mandatory Karpathy coverage, with Subcritical and McAteer occurrences merged once each. Published ebook compilation, with component print volumes verified by MIRI; not an unpublished blog reference. General epistemology and cognitive-bias explanation, not a specialist technical curriculum. Religious criticism and personal motivation are parts rather than the dominant purpose, so V7/V8 do not automatically apply. Miller praises useful reasoning material and discloses support for MIRI; Goertzel challenges the AI-risk framework. That disagreement does not by itself establish a veto on this broad compilation's central reasoning content. Do not treat contested quantum interpretation or AI claims as settled. Philosophy central, T12=-10. Not selected: very long, unevenly edited and disputed specialist applications.
notes: Useful probability reasoning mixed with confident extrapolations and psychological findings needing current verification.
